question: Which of these is a major cause of population displacement in northeast Nigeria?

options.A: Prolonged insurgency and violent conflict
options.B: Widespread industrial factory closures
options.C: Strict national immigration policy reforms
options.D: Government-mandated urban renewal projects

explanation: Sadly, ongoing conflict and insurgency in Nigeria's northeast have forced many families to flee their homes in search of safety.

question: An 8-month-old baby comes to the clinic having missed their 14-week doses. What should you do?

options.A: Restart the entire immunization series from the very beginning
options.B: Continue the schedule from where they stopped using catch-up principles
options.C: Give only adult-strength boosters to make up for lost time
options.D: Wait until the child turns one year old before administering any new vaccines

explanation: No need to restart! Immunization schedules are cumulative. Just use catch-up principles to pick up right where they left off.

question: What do we mean by "illness behaviour"?

options.A: The laboratory test results confirming an infection
options.B: The permanent physical damage caused by a disease
options.C: How a doctor chooses the correct medication dosage
options.D: How a person responds to symptoms and seeks help

explanation: Think of illness behaviour as the steps people take when something feels off in their body—ranging from staying home to rest, to visiting the clinic for help. You've got this!

question: What dangerous drug interaction must you warn patients about when taking ED meds like sildenafil (Viagra)?

options.A: Taking them with dairy products causes permanent blindness
options.B: Combining them with organic nitrates causes severe hypotension
options.C: Swallowing them with fruit juice stops their absorption entirely
options.D: Mixing them with aspirin causes sudden kidney failure

explanation: This is a classic clinical pearl! Both nitrates (for heart pain) and PDE5 inhibitors drop blood pressure. Taking them together can cause a life-threatening crash.

question: What purpose does the cork bung serve when using a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It filters out dust particles before the patient breathes the vapor
options.B: It seals the top of the jar so steam escapes only through the mouthpiece
options.C: It measures the exact temperature of the water inside the container
options.D: It absorbs excess medication that spills during preparation

explanation: Well done! The cork acts as a tight lid, making sure all the warm steam is forced to travel upward through the central tube and out the mouthpiece where the patient needs it.

question: If an abscess cavity has been packed with gauze, when is the patient usually asked to return for a check-up?

options.A: In one month for suture removal
options.B: Only if severe pain returns
options.C: After exactly two full weeks
options.D: Within 24 to 48 hours

explanation: Patients with packed wounds need a quick follow-up in 1 to 2 days so the healthcare team can check the healing and start removing the packing material.

question: A patient taking a strong muscle relaxant suddenly cannot pee. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: The medication dissolved the bladder lining.
options.B: The patient drank too much water too quickly.
options.C: The drug caused a sudden kidney infection.
options.D: The medication weakened the bladder muscle contraction.

explanation: Certain drugs can make the bladder muscle too weak to squeeze hard enough for you to empty it. Don't worry, pharmacology gets easier with practice!

question: A patient arrives at the emergency unit in status epilepticus (a seizure that won't stop). Which drug class should be given immediately to halt it?

options.A: Succinimides
options.B: Broad-spectrum agents
options.C: Benzodiazepines
options.D: Hydantoins

explanation: In an emergency, drugs like diazepam or lorazepam (benzodiazepines) work super fast to calm the brain down and stop a prolonged seizure. Quick action saves lives!

question: If a patient holds onto too much carbon dioxide because they aren't breathing deeply enough, what acid-base imbalance happens?

options.A: Respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic acidosis
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

explanation: Well done! Carbon dioxide acts like an acid in the body. If it builds up in the lungs, the blood becomes too acidic—hence respiratory acidosis.

question: At what exact times do we check a newborn's Apgar score?

options.A: At birth and every hour for four hours
options.B: At 5 and 10 minutes after birth
options.C: Immediately upon crowning and at delivery
options.D: At 1 and 5 minutes after birth

explanation: We check at 1 minute to see how the baby tolerated birth, and again at 5 minutes to see how they're adjusting to the outside world.

question: A nurse is getting ready to examine an anxious patient's external reproductive organs. What is the best first step?

options.A: Explain each step of the procedure before beginning
options.B: Begin the physical inspection immediately to save time
options.C: Skip the inspection if the patient expresses mild shyness
options.D: Ask family members to leave the room without explanation

explanation: Wonderful nursing instinct! Clear communication and gentle reassurance help ease patient anxiety during intimate checks.

question: Why should hospital management always consult frontline ward nurses when planning a new ward layout?

options.A: Nurses know practical workflow details like storage bottlenecks and blind spots
options.B: Nurses will personally fund the construction of the new nursing station
options.C: Nurses are legally required to sign off on all architectural blueprints
options.D: Nurses decide the overall construction budget for the entire hospital

explanation: You are the one working in the space every day! Consulting nurses helps catch practical issues—like where supplies should go—that architects might easily miss.

question: Which public health intervention quickly protects young children against severe Vitamin A deficiency during immunisation drives?

options.A: Teaching mothers how to boil drinking water
options.B: Distribution of deworming tablets only
options.C: Periodic Vitamin A capsule supplementation
options.D: Enforcing mandatory school feeding programs

explanation: Spot on! Giving high-dose Vitamin A capsules during routine immunization outreach is a fast, effective way to keep kids protected. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h6)

question: What is the typical acid-base blood gas state during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: Acute metabolic alkalosis
options.B: Uncompensated metabolic acidosis
options.C: Severe respiratory acidosis
options.D: Compensated respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Mums breathe off extra carbon dioxide, leading to mild respiratory alkalosis which the kidneys smoothly balance out with bicarbonate. Great revision!

question: What is the main goal of a rectal washout?

options.A: To measure the exact core body temperature
options.B: To administer liquid nutrition directly to the colon
options.C: To permanently cure chronic lower back pain
options.D: To completely cleanse the lower bowel using fluid cycles

explanation: Think of a rectal washout as a thorough internal clean. It uses repeated cycles of fluid to wash out stubborn stool and debris from the lower colon. You've got this!

question: Which of these is a classic example of a dependent nursing intervention in the ICU?

options.A: Assessing a patient's pain level using a standard rating scale
options.B: Providing basic hygiene care and bed baths
options.C: Titrating a continuous vasopressor drip per doctor's protocol
options.D: Turning a ventilated patient every two hours to prevent sores

explanation: Dependent means it depends on a doctor's order! Powerful drugs like vasopressors need a physician's backup before you can adjust them.

question: A patient reports severe burning and pain immediately after receiving ear drops. What is the nurse's first action?

options.A: Wait ten minutes to see if the pain goes away on its own
options.B: Stop the procedure and report the reaction to the doctor
options.C: Pack the ear canal tightly with sterile gauze
options.D: Reassure the patient and give a second dose right away

explanation: Severe pain means something is wrong, so the nurse must stop immediately and seek medical guidance. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h8)

question: Which group of medications is usually prescribed first for the long-term management of anxiety disorders?

options.A: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)
options.B: Short-acting skeletal muscle relaxants
options.C: Intravenous corticosteroid therapies
options.D: First-generation antipsychotic medications

explanation: You got it! SSRIs are the go-to choice for long-term anxiety care because they work well and have a safer side-effect profile.

question: What is the medical word for excessively heavy or long menstrual periods?

options.A: Menorrhagia
options.B: Amenorrhea
options.C: Dysmenorrhea
options.D: Menarche

explanation: You can remember this easily: 'Menorrhagia' means very heavy monthly flow that gets in the way of a woman's daily life and comfort.

question: What is the main job of extra protein during pregnancy?

options.A: Regulating sudden shifts in blood pressure
options.B: Preventing common digestive discomforts
options.C: Building uterine, breast, and fetal tissues
options.D: Providing quick energy for the mother's brain

explanation: Nailed it! Protein acts like the primary building blocks for the baby's growth, plus the mum's changing uterus and breasts.

question: What is a dangerous emergency complication for patients with high spinal cord injuries, often triggered by something simple like a full bladder?

options.A: Autonomic dysreflexia
options.B: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.C: Malignant hyperthermia
options.D: Acute respiratory alkalosis

explanation: That's right! Autonomic dysreflexia causes a sudden, life-threatening spike in blood pressure triggered by discomfort below the injury, such as a full bladder or tight clothing.

question: A weightlifter performing heavy one-rep maximum lifts relies primarily on which muscle fiber type?

options.A: Cardiac muscle fibers
options.B: Fast glycolytic fibers
options.C: Smooth muscle fibers
options.D: Slow oxidative fibers

explanation: Fast glycolytic fibers generate quick, powerful contractions using anaerobic pathways, perfect for heavy lifting and short sprints. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of the sutures and fontanelles in a foetal skull?

options.A: To increase the overall head size for brain growth
options.B: To allow the skull bones to overlap during birth
options.C: To prevent the brain from moving during delivery
options.D: To cool down the baby's brain temperature

explanation: The flexible joints and soft spots let the cranial bones shift and overlap, reducing head size so the baby can pass through the birth canal safely. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h1)

question: Why does the skin often look pale and feel cold when a person is bleeding heavily?

options.A: The heart stops pumping blood to the outer layers of skin entirely
options.B: Red blood cells turn blue when they lack oxygen in the skin
options.C: Blood vessels in the skin constrict to send blood to vital organs
options.D: Cold sweat cools down the surface temperature of the body

explanation: The body prioritizes the brain and heart during a crisis, narrowing skin blood vessels to save core circulation. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T4#GNS123_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is your very first priority when a poisoned patient arrives in the emergency unit?

options.A: Asking family members about the patient's financial history
options.B: Stabilizing vital functions using the ABCDE approach
options.C: Administering a broad-spectrum antidote immediately
options.D: Inducing vomiting to empty the stomach contents

explanation: Safety first! Always check Airway, Breathing, and Circulation (ABCDE) before trying to figure out exactly what poison was swallowed.

question: Where should you position the steam generator in relation to the patient's bed?

options.A: Underneath the mattress for hidden warmth
options.B: Tied securely to the side rail of the crib
options.C: At a safe distance to prevent accidental burns
options.D: Directly inside the tent canopy next to the pillow

explanation: Safety first! Always keep the hot generator far enough away to protect the patient from burns.

question: Why is checking drug compatibility important when administering multiple intravenous infusions?

options.A: Incompatible drugs can react and form solid crystals that block the catheter
options.B: Combining medications changes the colour of the plastic infusion tubing
options.C: Mixing drugs always causes the patient to develop a skin rash
options.D: Incompatible solutions neutralize each other and make nurses look careless

explanation: Chemical reactions between mixed drugs can create precipitates that clog the line and endanger the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why must a tiny opening be deliberately left when performing infibulation?

options.A: To ensure future surgical procedures are easier to perform
options.B: To allow the passage of urine and menstrual blood
options.C: To allow air circulation inside the reproductive tract
options.D: To prevent complete closure of the abdominal cavity

explanation: Even with infibulation, a small opening is necessary so that essential body fluids like urine and menses can still leave the body.

question: What is the main job of your eustachian tube when you yawn or swallow on a flight?

options.A: To amplify high-frequency sound waves
options.B: To translate fluid waves into nerve impulses
options.C: To equalize air pressure in the middle ear
options.D: To produce earwax for protection

explanation: That "pop" you feel in your ears when swallowing helps the eustachian tube let air in or out, keeping the pressure balanced on both sides of your eardrum.

question: How is the Hepatitis A virus mainly spread from person to person?

options.A: Through infected blood transfusions
options.B: Via unprotected sexual contact
options.C: Through the fecal-oral route
options.D: By mosquito or insect bites

explanation: Hepatitis A spreads easily when someone accidentally ingests food or water that has been contaminated with tiny amounts of infected stool. Good hand hygiene is key!

question: When is it legally and ethically okay for a nurse to share a patient's confidential abuse details?

options.A: At any time the nurse feels curious about the case details
options.B: When there is a mandatory legal requirement or imminent danger to life
options.C: Whenever family members demand information about the incident
options.D: When posting general hospital statistics on social media

explanation: Spot on! Patient privacy is sacred, but we must break confidentiality if someone's life is in immediate danger or the law requires mandatory reporting.

question: A patient spends an hour doing a hand-washing ritual before meals. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Allow time for the ritual initially, then work with the patient to gradually set limits
options.B: Immediately shut off the water supply and force the patient to sit at the table
options.C: Administer a stat dose of intravenous antipsychotic medication to stop the habit
options.D: Scold the patient firmly to teach them that the behavior is completely useless

explanation: Spot on! Never cut them off cold turkey right away. Give them time at first, then gently help them reduce it over time.

question: How is a Stage 1 pressure sore best identified on light-skinned patients?

options.A: Intact skin with redness that does not turn white when pressed
options.B: An open crater exposing subcutaneous fat and muscle
options.C: A black, hard scab covering deep tissue damage
options.D: A shallow pink wound with clear fluid drainage

explanation: In Stage 1, the skin isn't broken yet, but it shows redness that stays red even when you press a finger on it (non-blanching). Good to know for your ward rotations! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which tool do we use specifically to measure pressure inside the eye?

options.A: Ophthalmoscope
options.B: Snellen chart
options.C: Otoscope
options.D: Tonometer

explanation: A tonometer checks the fluid pressure inside the eye, which is a key way nurses and doctors screen for glaucoma.

question: How does proper birth spacing directly help keep mothers safe?

options.A: By reducing complications like severe bleeding and exhausted uterine muscles
options.B: By ensuring all deliveries happen exclusively at home
options.C: By guaranteeing that mothers will never experience morning sickness
options.D: By completely eliminating the need for antenatal care visits

explanation: You've got this! Proper spacing gives the uterus time to rest between pregnancies, which greatly lowers the risk of heavy bleeding (hemorrhage). Great nursing insight to keep in mind!

question: How many signal functions must a health facility perform to be called a BEmOC center?

options.A: Three signal functions
options.B: Ten signal functions
options.C: Twelve signal functions
options.D: Seven signal functions

explanation: To be officially recognized as a Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC) center, a facility must be able to handle all seven specific medical interventions.

question: How do Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs) differ from basic ADLs?

options.A: IADLs involve more complex tasks needed to live independently in the community.
options.B: IADLs require no thinking, just muscle strength.
options.C: IADLs are learned before basic self-care.
options.D: IADLs only focus on physical hygiene.

explanation: Think of basic ADLs as surviving day-to-day, while IADLs are the next level up—like cooking, shopping, and handling money—that help someone live on their own.

question: What is the medical term for the crunching sound when broken bone ends rub together?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Crepitus
options.C: Contracture
options.D: Clonus

explanation: Crepitus is that distinct crunching sound or feeling you get when jagged ends of a broken bone grind against each other. It's a classic sign nurses listen and feel for during assessments!

question: When is the final routine post-natal visit usually scheduled to ensure the reproductive organs have fully recovered?

options.A: After one year
options.B: At 24 hours
options.C: On day 3
options.D: Between 4 and 6 weeks

explanation: The 4 to 6-week mark wraps up the puerperium! It's the perfect time for you to confirm the womb has gone back to normal size and chat about family planning.

question: What is a major risk if a nurse crosses professional boundaries with a home care patient?

options.A: Improving the patient's physical healing speed instantly
options.B: Eliminating all paperwork requirements for the visit
options.C: Guaranteeing a promotion from the nursing agency
options.D: Compromising clinical objectivity and causing burnout

explanation: Well done! When boundaries get blurry, it's easy to lose your professional focus, which leads to emotional fatigue and can affect the quality of your care.

question: What is the main physical process that moves water between body fluid compartments?

options.A: Active transport
options.B: Filtration
options.C: Diffusion of proteins
options.D: Osmosis

explanation: Great job! Think of osmosis as water's way of flowing toward areas with a higher concentration of solutes to keep things balanced.

question: What is the main use of calcium carbonate when taken as a mineral supplement?

options.A: Lowering high blood pressure through direct vasodilation
options.B: Neutralizing stomach acid and supporting bone strength
options.C: Stopping acute seizures in pregnant women with eclampsia
options.D: Thinning thick mucus secretions in the respiratory tract

explanation: Calcium carbonate doubles as a handy antacid for the tummy and provides essential calcium to build strong bones!

question: Which common, lightweight device uses two small prongs to deliver low-flow oxygen right into a patient's nostrils?

options.A: Non-rebreather mask
options.B: Venturi mask
options.C: Nasal cannula
options.D: Simple face mask

explanation: You'll see nasal cannulas everywhere in the ward! They're the standard, comfortable choice for giving patients a little extra oxygen through their nose.

question: What is considered the gold standard method for continuously tracking births and deaths in a country?

options.A: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS)
options.B: Annual social media health awareness polls
options.C: Quarterly traditional healer reports
options.D: Random telephone interviews with local market women

explanation: A complete CRVS system is the ideal, continuous method for recording every vital event as it happens across the entire population.

question: A client considering a tubal ligation is worried it will ruin her sex life and stop her periods. What should you tell her?

options.A: Explain that the surgery only blocks the tubes and does not affect hormones, sexual desire, or menstrual cycles
options.B: Agree that she will enter early menopause and lose all sexual interest immediately
options.C: Tell her that her periods will stop completely because her ovaries will be removed
options.D: Suggest she use emergency contraceptive pills instead of surgery forever

explanation: As a nurse, part of your job is reassurance! Tubal ligation only blocks the path for the egg and sperm; her ovaries stay safe and keep producing her normal hormones.

question: A patient asks how to prevent stomach upset during stressful exams. What is your best response?

options.A: Tell the patient that stress has no impact on digestion
options.B: Suggest taking heavy sleeping pills during the daytime hours
options.C: Encourage stress reduction techniques and regular balanced meals
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating completely until stress ends

explanation: Stress really does mess with your tummy! Helping patients manage stress and stick to regular meals protects their gut from acting up.

question: A community health nurse opens a delivery kit and finds a soap bar, a plastic sheet, a cord tie, a razor blade, and a cloth. What is the primary role of the razor blade?

options.A: To open other plastic packaging
options.B: To rupture the amniotic sac
options.C: To clean the mother's skin
options.D: To cut the umbilical cord

explanation: The razor blade serves as the sterile instrument dedicated to cutting the umbilical cord cleanly. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h2)

question: Which head measurement presents when the baby's head is tilted all the way back in a brow presentation, making delivery very difficult?

options.A: Suboccipitobregmatic diameter
options.B: Occipitofrontal diameter
options.C: Biparietal diameter
options.D: Mentovertical diameter

explanation: Spot on! At 13.5 cm, the mentovertical diameter is the widest one, and it's usually too big to easily pass through an average pelvis.

question: Which agency coordinates primary healthcare development at the national level in Nigeria?

options.A: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Nigerian Medical Association (NMA)

explanation: The NPHCDA is the main federal body guiding PHC implementation all across Nigeria. Good to know for Nigerian nursing practice!

question: What do we call the reply a listener gives back to a speaker during a chat?

options.A: Encoding
options.B: The channel
options.C: Feedback
options.D: Decoding

explanation: That's right! Feedback is simply the response that lets you know if the other person truly caught your message.

question: What is a major nursing concern when an older adult has severe dental problems and missing teeth?

options.A: Increased likelihood of developing hypertension
options.B: Rapid cognitive decline within forty-eight hours
options.C: Immediate kidney failure due to poor digestion
options.D: Risk of malnutrition and difficulty chewing certain foods

explanation: When chewing hurts or is difficult, residents might skip healthy foods like meat and raw veggies unless their meals are specially prepared. You are learning great clinical foresight!

question: What is the very first thing you should do when setting new objectives for a healthcare unit?

options.A: Punish staff members who failed previous targets.
options.B: Purchase expensive new medical equipment for the ward.
options.C: Assess current performance using past data and audit reports.
options.D: Rewrite the entire hospital mission statement.

explanation: Before moving forward, we always check where we currently stand by reviewing past records and audits to see what needs fixing.

question: What kind of values go on the vertical y-axis when you draw an ogive?

options.A: Cumulative frequencies
options.B: Individual patient names
options.C: Class midpoint averages
options.D: Raw unadded frequencies

explanation: Exactly! The vertical axis is always reserved for the running total, which is our cumulative frequency.

question: What is the main feature that separates stable angina from unstable angina?

options.A: Stable angina lasts for days without any relief
options.B: Unstable angina is always completely cured with exercise
options.C: Unstable angina occurs unpredictably even at rest
options.D: Stable angina causes pain that radiates down both legs

explanation: While stable angina follows a predictable pattern during exertion, unstable angina can happen at rest and represents a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why should you still talk and explain procedures to a sedated patient on a ventilator?

options.A: It satisfies the legal requirement for written informed consent
options.B: It helps the mechanical ventilator synchronize with the patient's heart
options.C: Unconscious or sedated patients may still perceive and process sound
options.D: Hospital regulations require talking to every patient on a machine

explanation: Hearing is often the last sense to go. Explaining what you are doing is a kind, human act that helps soothe fear and confusion.

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To provide free medications to all visiting patients
options.B: To maintain a continuous supply of essential drugs through sales revenue
options.C: To fund the construction of new hospital wards and laboratories
options.D: To generate profit for the hospital management board

explanation: Think of the DRF like a self-sustaining cycle! Money from drug sales is used right back to buy fresh stock, so the pharmacy never runs dry.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a secondary (acquired) immunodeficiency?

options.A: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
options.B: Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID)
options.C: A pollen allergy (Type 1 Hypersensitivity)
options.D: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection

explanation: HIV is acquired later in life. It slowly damages the immune system over time, which makes it a secondary immunodeficiency rather than something you are born with.

question: How is neonatal tetanus mainly diagnosed in clinical practice?

options.A: Routine magnetic resonance imaging scans
options.B: Positive blood culture results for the virus
options.C: Elevated white blood cell counts in urine
options.D: Physical examination and clinical history

explanation: You're doing great! Doctors and nurses diagnose it based on the baby's history—a normal birth followed by sudden stiffness, muscle spasms, and trouble feeding.

question: What is a common health problem in children who eat a poor, low-diversity diet?

options.A: Complete immunity to common childhood tropical diseases
options.B: Rapid increase in bone density and excessive height
options.C: Sudden development of high blood pressure in infancy
options.D: Increased vulnerability to infections and stunted physical growth

explanation: That's right. Missing out on diverse nutrients weakens their immune system and slows down their growth, leading to frequent illnesses.

question: What must a germ do inside the body before you finally start feeling sick?

options.A: Trigger an immediate allergic reaction
options.B: Stimulate the production of red blood cells
options.C: Cause permanent failure of the lymphatic system
options.D: Multiply and reach a sufficient infectious dose

explanation: Spot on. The germs have to quietly copy themselves and build up in numbers before they can trigger noticeable symptoms.

question: Why do hospital policies play a big role in what you are allowed to do during clinicals?

options.A: They dictate what nursing students are legally permitted to perform on patients
options.B: They set the tuition fees for the university nursing department
options.C: They determine the exact colors of the school uniforms
options.D: They write all the final examinations for the nursing council

explanation: Hospitals have strict rules to protect patients and keep student practice within safe, legal boundaries.

question: When do we usually rely on indirect sources of data to track maternal mortality?

options.A: When international donors refuse to look at hospital logbooks
options.B: When civil registration systems are incomplete or non-functional
options.C: When every single pregnant woman delivers inside a tertiary clinic
options.D: When hospitals have too much digital data to process manually

explanation: In many areas, births and deaths happen at home and aren't captured by official government books. That's when indirect methods become a lifesaver for getting accurate statistics!

question: Which of these statements about injectable contraceptives is FALSE?

options.A: They prevent pregnancy by stopping ovulation
options.B: They require regular repeat doses to remain effective
options.C: They lead to permanent sterility after one dose
options.D: They can cause changes in monthly bleeding patterns

explanation: Injectables do not cause permanent infertility! Once you stop, fertility naturally returns after the drug clears the system.

question: Why do oxygen cylinders and wall outlets always need strict 'No Smoking' safety signs nearby?

options.A: Oxygen strongly supports combustion and makes fires spread rapidly
options.B: Tobacco smoke clogs the small holes in the nasal cannula prongs
options.C: Smoking interferes with the machine's internal electrical circuits
options.D: The smell of smoke ruins the purity of the medical gas supply

explanation: Oxygen itself doesn't burn, but it feeds fires aggressively. Even a tiny spark can turn into a massive flame in seconds around supplemental oxygen!

question: What is the proper way to cut fingernails during routine care?

options.A: In a rounded shape with deep side corners
options.B: As short as possible down to the quick
options.C: In a deep V-shape to expose the nail bed
options.D: Straight across following the natural curve

explanation: Great thinking! Cutting straight across and avoiding digging into the corners helps protect your patient from painful ingrown nails.

question: What is the main way that antiemetic (anti-nausea) drugs stop vomiting?

options.A: Blocking specific neurotransmitter receptors
options.B: Destroying circulating toxins in the blood
options.C: Enhancing gastric motility and emptying
options.D: Increasing blood flow to the medulla oblongata

explanation: You nailed it! Anti-nausea meds work by latching onto and blocking the chemical receptors along the vomiting pathway so the brain doesn't get the 'throw up' signal. Keep it up!

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier stopping women from using post-abortion contraception?

options.A: Fear of unpleasant side effects
options.B: Lack of transport to the clinic
options.C: Guaranteed 100 percent long-term effectiveness
options.D: High product costs at the pharmacy

explanation: High effectiveness is a great thing! Fear, cost, and travel issues are the real hurdles patients face.

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of health education in community nursing?

options.A: To empower individuals and groups to adopt healthy lifestyles
options.B: To diagnose complex medical disorders in hospital laboratories
options.C: To prescribe pharmaceutical drugs without a doctor's order
options.D: To generate revenue for local government health departments

explanation: Health education gives people the knowledge and skills they need to make healthy choices and prevent illnesses. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h6)

question: Which agency sets and enforces the main federal regulations for skilled nursing facilities?

options.A: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
options.B: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
options.C: World Health Organization (WHO)
options.D: National Institutes of Health (NIH)

explanation: CMS oversees the federal rules and quality standards that certified skilled nursing facilities must follow. You're building a strong regulatory foundation!

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for twice in the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Symptom and Staff
options.B: Situation and Assessment
options.C: Support and Solution
options.D: Situation and Safety

explanation: SBAR stands for Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation, which is used for structured clinical handovers. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h4)

question: What is your very first priority action if you suspect a patient is having an idiosyncratic drug reaction?

options.A: Wait for laboratory confirmation before acting
options.B: Increase the drug dose to build up a tolerance
options.C: Give the patient a strong dose of antihistamines
options.D: Stop the offending medication immediately

explanation: Rule number one of drug safety: if a medication is causing harm, stop giving it right away to protect your patient from further injury!

question: What is a major reason food gets lost before it ever reaches the local market?

options.A: Excessive consumer demand in urban centers
options.B: High levels of crop diversity on small farms
options.C: Poor storage facilities and bad transport roads
options.D: Strict government food safety inspections

explanation: Bad roads and poor storage mean a lot of harvest spoils before getting to people who need it. A very real challenge in many regions!

question: Your surgical mask becomes damp and sweaty during a busy shift. What should you do?

options.A: Leave it on because moisture helps filtration
options.B: Flip it inside out so the dry side faces out
options.C: Remove and discard it, clean your hands, and put on a fresh one
options.D: Wipe it with paper towels and pocket it

explanation: Once a mask gets damp, its filter barrier stops working well. Swap it out for a fresh one to stay safe!

question: Which harmful traditional practice should nurses actively discourage when teaching mothers about diarrhoea?

options.A: Mixing ORS packets in clean drinking water
options.B: Withholding food and fluids to rest the bowel
options.C: Continuing to breastfeed the infant on demand
options.D: Giving zinc supplements for two full weeks

explanation: Never starve a tummy bug! Stopping food and water only makes malnutrition and dehydration worse. Children with diarrhoea need continued feeding and plenty of fluids to heal.

question: Why do fungal scalp infections like ringworm (tinea capitis) usually need oral medication instead of just medicated shampoo?

options.A: Shampoos cannot easily penetrate deep into the hair follicle where the fungus lives
options.B: Oral medications are cheaper and easier for hospitalized patients to swallow
options.C: Medicated shampoos will permanently damage the texture of the hair shaft
options.D: Fungal infections on the head are completely unaffected by topical treatments

explanation: Washing the surface isn't always enough because the fungus digs deep inside the hair follicle where shampoos can't easily reach. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h5)

question: A patient has a large ovarian cyst and complains of a dull ache and needing to pee very often. Why is she experiencing frequent urination?

options.A: Her kidneys are producing extra urine due to stress
options.B: The cyst is pressing against her urinary bladder
options.C: The infection from the cyst has spread to her kidneys
options.D: Her hormone levels are causing her to drink more water

explanation: It's all about anatomy! A big cyst takes up space in the pelvis and pushes right against the bladder, making her feel the urge to go more often.

question: Where does blood go immediately after leaving the right side of the newborn's heart?

options.A: To the lungs
options.B: To the liver
options.C: To the placenta
options.D: To the brain

explanation: The right side of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary arteries directly to the lungs for oxygen. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: What is one effective nursing action during a multidisciplinary ward round?

options.A: Writing new drug orders without consulting the attending doctor
options.B: Hiding the prescription chart from the medical team
options.C: Discharging all patients who take more than two tablets daily
options.D: Questioning unnecessary prescriptions and suggesting alternatives

explanation: Nurses act as safety advocates by speaking up when a medication order appears unsafe or clinically unjustified. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T7#GNS215_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the medical term for uncoordinated, clumsy muscle movements caused by a problem in the cerebellum?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Anosognosia
options.C: Ataxia
options.D: Aphasia

explanation: Ataxia simply means a lack of smooth muscle coordination, resulting in those jerky, unsteady movements we see in cerebellar issues. You're learning core clinical terms like a pro!

question: Which family caregiver is at the highest risk for caregiver burnout and potentially committing abuse?

options.A: A relative who visits once a week to help with grocery shopping
options.B: A professional nurse who rotates shifts at an assisted living facility
options.C: A spouse who hires a home health aide to assist four hours a day
options.D: An adult child providing 24-hour care alone with no respite support

explanation: Carrying the heavy load 24/7 without a break easily leads to severe burnout. Supporting caregivers is part of holistic nursing!

question: What is the primary goal of using strict aseptic technique during invasive procedures?

options.A: To neutralize chemical toxins released by resident skin flora
options.B: To eliminate all pathogenic microorganisms from the sterile field
options.C: To reduce the total number of bacteria on non-porous furniture
options.D: To remove visible dirt and oil from the patient's outer skin

explanation: Aseptic technique aims to protect susceptible body sites by ensuring zero pathogens are introduced during invasive tasks. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h7)

question: A nurse notices that a postoperative surgical wound is increasingly red, warm, and draining foul-smelling pus. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the patient's scheduled discharge day to mention it
options.B: Assume this is a normal healing process and take no action
options.C: Report the findings and document them clearly for the care team
options.D: Apply a dry bandage and advise the patient not to look at it

explanation: Prompt reporting and documentation ensure the medical team can investigate and treat a potential surgical site infection early. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: Where in the digestive tract does the absorption of almost all nutrients happen?

options.A: Esophagus
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Large intestine
options.D: Small intestine

explanation: The small intestine is the superstar of absorption! Its lining is specially designed to soak up digested nutrients straight into the bloodstream.

question: What problem do instructional materials help reduce by giving students a concrete picture of a concept?

options.A: Verbalism
options.B: Dehydration
options.C: Hypertension
options.D: Somnolence

explanation: Verbalism happens when students use or hear words without truly understanding what they mean, which teaching aids prevent by showing the actual object or process. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h2)

question: What usually happens right away to a community when its food supply chain breaks down?

options.A: Lower rates of chronic illness among residents
options.B: The permanent closure of all local hospitals
options.C: An immediate surplus of fresh vegetables in every market
options.D: Food scarcity and sudden price inflation

explanation: When transport and supply routes fail, food becomes hard to find, and whatever is left usually shoots up in price.

question: Why do midwives and doctors check a baby's fontanelles and sutures during labour?

options.A: To estimate the exact gestational age of the pregnancy
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the foetus before delivery
options.C: To figure out the position and attitude of the baby's head
options.D: To check if the baby's brain is developing normally in utero

explanation: By feeling these soft spots and lines, you can map out which way the baby's head is facing and how well it is flexing to come down.

question: Which scenario represents a violation of the 'right time' medication principle?

options.A: Crushing a simple uncoated tablet for a patient who cannot swallow pills
options.B: Giving a routine morning antibiotic two hours late without a valid reason
options.C: Documenting the medication immediately after the patient swallows it
options.D: Checking the patient's identification band before opening the package

explanation: Administering medications significantly outside their scheduled time frame can cause blood levels to drop too low or spike too high. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h5)

question: A newly qualified nurse performs a minor surgical procedure meant only for doctors, just to save time. What is the legal implication of this?

options.A: It is permitted under emergency hospital bylaws everywhere.
options.B: It constitutes practicing outside the legal scope of nursing.
options.C: It automatically upgrades the nurse's license to a medical one.
options.D: It is acceptable if the patient recovers without complications.

explanation: Always stay within your professional boundary! Doing tasks reserved for other professions violates NMCN regulations and can lead to serious disciplinary actions.

question: Which part of the brain acts as the emotional alarm system that triggers the fight-or-flight response during anxiety?

options.A: The pituitary gland
options.B: The cerebellum
options.C: The medulla oblongata
options.D: The amygdala

explanation: Spot on! The amygdala is our emotional radar. It processes threats and sounds the alarm early when we feel anxious. You've got this!

question: Which kitchen habit helps prevent accidental grease or boiling water spills?

options.A: Using metal spoons for all cooking tasks
options.B: Turning pot handles inward toward the stove back
options.C: Leaving burners on high heat while cleaning
options.D: Placing hot oil pans near the edge of the counter

explanation: Turning handles inward keeps pots out of reach of children and prevents adults from accidentally bumping into them. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h4)

question: A man and a woman of the same weight each have two standard drinks. What is the most likely result?

options.A: The male patient will absorb the alcohol much faster than the female patient
options.B: Neither patient will absorb any alcohol into their systemic circulation
options.C: The female patient will have a noticeably higher blood alcohol concentration
options.D: Both patients will have the exact same blood alcohol concentration

explanation: Body composition matters! Differences in body water and metabolism mean women generally hit higher blood alcohol levels than men from the exact same drink.

question: What measuring device should nurses recommend for giving liquid medicines safely to children?

options.A: A plastic coffee stirrer
options.B: An oral dosing syringe
options.C: A large soup ladle
options.D: A standard kitchen teaspoon

explanation: Oral syringes give precise dosing accuracy, whereas regular kitchen spoons vary wildly in size and liquid capacity.

question: Which medication group forms the first step of the WHO analgesic ladder?

options.A: Strong agonists like fentanyl
options.B: Pure antagonists like naloxone
options.C: Intravenous muscle relaxants
options.D: Non-opioids like paracetamol

explanation: For mild pain, we always start simple at Step One with basic non-opioids like paracetamol or ibuprofen, plus an adjuvant if needed.

question: Why are midwives in remote Nigerian health clinics allowed to give certain emergency drugs on their own?

options.A: Doctors are often unavailable during urgent obstetric situations
options.B: Standard hospital policy prohibits doctors from prescribing to newborns
options.C: Midwives complete more medical pharmacology training than doctors
options.D: Pharmacies are legally banned from stocking maternal medications

explanation: You've got this! In remote areas where a doctor might not be around, midwives need the power to act fast and save lives.

question: An LTC nurse spends a big part of the shift supervising nursing assistants. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: To minimize direct nurse interaction with residents
options.B: To ensure delegated tasks are performed safely and correctly
options.C: To complete administrative paperwork required by the hospital
options.D: To replace the need for formal care planning meetings

explanation: You got it! As the professional nurse, you lead the care team and oversee assistants to make sure daily tasks like hygiene and safety are done properly.

question: Where should a used injection needle go immediately after you give an injection?

options.A: Inside your pocket until you reach the utility room
options.B: Directly into a puncture-resistant safety box
options.C: Back into the original plastic wrapper on the desk
options.D: On top of the medication tray for later sorting

explanation: Always drop sharps straight into a designated safety box kept right beside you. Never carry them around or leave them on trays!

question: When doing an ear check on an adult using an otoscope, how should you pull the outer ear (pinna) to straighten the canal?

options.A: Tilt the patient's head forward
options.B: Push the tragus inward firmly
options.C: Pull the earlobe straight down
options.D: Pull the pinna up and back

explanation: You've got it! Pulling the pinna up and back straightens out the adult ear canal so you can get a clear view of the eardrum. (For kids, remember you pull down and back!)

question: What is cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Fluid or blood filling the sac around the heart and squeezing it
options.B: Widening of the lower belly aorta
options.C: Inflammation of the inner heart valves
options.D: A blood clot blocking a coronary artery

explanation: Imagine water balloon pressure around the heart. When fluid leaks into the pericardial sac, it builds up pressure so the heart chambers can't relax and fill properly.

question: What term describes the natural slowing down of immune system function as a person grows older?

options.A: Immunodeficiency
options.B: Immunosenescence
options.C: Seroconversion
options.D: Hypersensitivity

explanation: Immunosenescence simply means 'immune aging.' Just like muscles get tired, our immune response naturally softens as we age. Great word to add to your nursing vocabulary!

question: How do risk assessment findings help local primary health care centers?

options.A: By allowing them to close down clinics with low patient numbers
options.B: By removing the need to keep paper medical records for patients
options.C: By automatically increasing the monthly salary of the clinic staff
options.D: By guiding them to direct scarce medical supplies where most needed

explanation: Resources are usually limited in our clinics. Clear data helps community nurses send drugs and mosquito nets precisely where the greatest need is.

question: Why must anticholinergic anti-spasmodics be strictly avoided in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma?

options.A: They paralyze the muscles that move the eyeball
options.B: They dry out the tear ducts completely
options.C: They cause permanent blindness within one hour
options.D: They can dangerously increase eye pressure

explanation: Anticholinergics affect how the eye drains fluid. In glaucoma patients, this can trigger a dangerous spike in pressure inside the eye.

question: Why are community health nurses usually the first to notice an unusual disease cluster?

options.A: Because they only review paperwork sent from foreign countries
options.B: Because they spend all their time working in national research labs
options.C: Because they focus entirely on hospital financial accounting
options.D: Because they interact daily with families and local groups

explanation: Community nurses are right on the ground! Because you work closely with local families every day, you're in the best position to spot when something feels off.

question: What do we call a disease that is always present at a steady, expected level in a specific community?

options.A: A pandemic disease
options.B: An epidemic disease
options.C: An endemic disease
options.D: A sporadic disease

explanation: You've got this! An endemic disease hangs around at a predictable, steady level in a specific area—like malaria in many parts of Nigeria—without causing sudden panic.

question: How do accurate nursing medication records help support the DRF scheme?

options.A: They allow the hospital to charge patients double for every injection
options.B: They help pharmacists accurately forecast future drug consumption needs
options.C: They replace the need for physical stock counts in the pharmacy
options.D: They prove to the nursing council that staff are writing clearly

explanation: Wonderful! Clear records from the wards show exactly what patients are using, helping the pharmacy order the right amounts without guesswork.

question: Which living organisms are commonly used as 'factories' in biotechnology to make drugs?

options.A: Bacteria or yeast cells
options.B: Cattle and laboratory mice
options.C: Insects and earthworms
options.D: Poppy and foxglove plants

explanation: Scientists use tiny living things like bacteria or yeast, giving them a little genetic upgrade to safely churn out human proteins like insulin.

question: What is a common problem with social welfare systems for people with disabilities in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Bureaucracy is fast and fully digital
options.B: Government healthcare is entirely free and comprehensive
options.C: Benefits are often sporadic, underfunded, and hard to access
options.D: Every citizen gets a guaranteed lifelong pension

explanation: Good policies might exist on paper, but in reality, government support systems are often too weak or irregular to rely on.

question: Why should we educate religious and traditional leaders about Youth Friendly Services?

options.A: It allows local leaders to diagnose minor ailments
options.B: It stops community members from spreading myths and stigma
options.C: It forces parents to pay for youth medications
options.D: It eliminates the need for professional nurses

explanation: Spot on! Bringing community leaders on board builds trust and clears up the myth that YFS encourages promiscuity instead of health.

question: What is the main benefit of keeping accurate records of workplace injuries and close calls?

options.A: It helps identify dangerous trends and prevents future accidents
options.B: It guarantees that the business will never face taxation
options.C: It allows employers to hide safety violations from inspectors
options.D: It replaces the need to provide medical treatment to victims

explanation: Reviewing past injury logs helps safety teams spot repeating problems so they can fix them before anyone else gets hurt.

question: Which airway maneuver should you use if you think your patient has a neck or spine injury?

options.A: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.B: Lateral neck rotation
options.C: Rapid neck hyperextension
options.D: Head-tilt, chin-lift maneuver

explanation: The jaw-thrust opens the airway without bending or moving the neck, keeping the cervical spine safe from further harm. Brilliant nursing judgment!

question: How does hyperemesis gravidarum differ from normal pregnancy morning sickness?

options.A: It only occurs during the final trimester of pregnancy
options.B: It causes severe, unstoppable vomiting leading to dehydration and weight loss
options.C: It has no effect on the overall fluid balance of the body
options.D: It usually resolves completely within the first four weeks

explanation: While normal morning sickness is manageable, hyperemesis involves nonstop vomiting that drains the body's fluids and nutrition. Great job keeping the clinical differences clear!

question: What should a nurse do immediately if the physical count of pethidine does not match the register balance?

options.A: Add personal money to replace any missing tablets
options.B: Wait until the next shift to see if the count balances out
options.C: Report the discrepancy right away to the nursing supervisor
options.D: Cross out the wrong number and write a new one quietly

explanation: Missing drugs could indicate theft or error, requiring immediate official investigation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h7)

question: A rural health clinic in Nigeria runs out of basic antibiotics due to weak local distribution. Which national strategy is failing in this specific instance?

options.A: The regulation of surgical equipment manufacturing standards
options.B: The curriculum used to train primary school teachers
options.C: The Essential Drug Policy supply chain and distribution network
options.D: The enforcement of international luxury hotel taxation

explanation: Stockouts at rural clinics highlight flaws in the procurement and distribution mechanisms outlined by the national drug policy. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)

question: When should the cancer rehabilitation process ideally start?

options.A: Only after chemotherapy is fully completed
options.B: At the time of cancer diagnosis
options.C: After permanent disabilities develop
options.D: When the patient enters palliative care

explanation: Starting early is key! When we begin rehab right from diagnosis, we can stop long-term physical problems before they even start.

question: What is a common myth that scares young people away from hormonal contraception?

options.A: It automatically increases an individual's height by ten inches
options.B: It turns eye color into a completely different shade overnight
options.C: It causes permanent internal accumulation or organ rotting
options.D: It cures all forms of infectious diseases instantly

explanation: Baseless fears about pills piling up inside the body are common myths. Patient education clears this right up!

question: How does school-based health education impact the wider community?

options.A: Parents lose responsibility for teaching their children
options.B: Communities stop building local health clinics entirely
options.C: Local hospitals experience a permanent drop in staffing
options.D: Children take healthy habits home to their families

explanation: Students act as health messengers, sharing hygiene and nutrition practices learned at school with their families at home. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h6)

question: A newly admitted patient is shaking before a scheduled biopsy. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Frustration over wearing a standard hospital gown
options.B: Disappointment with the hospital meal schedule
options.C: Anticipation of pain and uncertainty about the diagnosis
options.D: Annoyance with noisy roommates in the ward

explanation: You're right! Not knowing what the results will be, coupled with the worry of physical pain, is a classic recipe for procedure anxiety.

question: Which skin antiseptic keeps working for hours after you apply it?

options.A: Glutaraldehyde
options.B: Sodium hypochlorite
options.C: Chlorhexidine gluconate
options.D: Isopropyl alcohol

explanation: Spot on! Chlorhexidine sticks to the skin and keeps killing bacteria long after you put it on, which is why we love it for surgical scrubs.

question: What is a primary responsibility of a community health nurse in preventing infectious diseases?

options.A: Manufacturing sterile surgical instruments in the clinic kitchen
options.B: Isolating entire towns when a single flu case is reported
options.C: Educating families on hygiene, sanitation, and vaccination
options.D: Prescribing high-dose antibiotics without consulting a doctor

explanation: Community nurses empower everyday people with the practical knowledge needed to stop infections at home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h8)

question: A community nurse is writing a report about job hunting and financial independence among 22-year-olds. Which term is best to use?

options.A: Puberty
options.B: Toddlerhood
options.C: Youth
options.D: Adolescent

explanation: Since the focus is on jobs and independence for a 22-year-old, 'youth' is the most accurate and professional term to use.

question: Why must a 24-hour emergency phone number be on hazardous material shipping documents?

options.A: To provide immediate expert guidance if a spill or exposure occurs
options.B: To let the receiving nurse ask about patient clinical history
options.C: To schedule the exact pickup time for the next laboratory batch
options.D: To allow the courier to confirm the payment receipt with accounting

explanation: If there's an accident on the road, emergency responders need someone to call instantly who knows how to handle that specific hazard safely.

question: What is a primary clinical feature of hemodynamic instability?

options.A: High fever with shivering and chills
options.B: Elevated urine output above normal limits
options.C: Gradual weight gain over several weeks
options.D: Inadequate blood flow to vital organs

explanation: Hemodynamic instability simply means the circulation is failing to supply enough blood to keep organs working properly. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which supplement is most important to give before pregnancy to help prevent birth defects?

options.A: Potassium chloride
options.B: Folic acid
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Calcium carbonate

explanation: Folic acid is a superstar vitamin! Taking it before and during early pregnancy greatly lowers the risk of neural tube defects like spina bifida. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: A patient is fighting a bad malaria infection. Which food group should you encourage to boost their immune system?

options.A: Body-building foods like large amounts of table salt
options.B: Energy-giving foods like pure sugar and palm oil
options.C: Protective foods like oranges and spinach
options.D: Non-perishable foods like canned dry biscuits

explanation: Spot on! Fruits and veggies are 'protective' because their vitamins and minerals boost immunity and help the body fight off infections.

question: A PAC patient is stable and ready to go home. What is the best next step for the nurse?

options.A: Provide compassionate contraceptive counseling and discharge instructions
options.B: Withhold discharge until a family elder arrives to sign papers
options.C: Scold the patient so she does not experience complications again
options.D: Prescribe heavy sedatives to prevent emotional processing

explanation: Before they leave, always give clear discharge notes and friendly, non-judgmental advice on how to prevent another unplanned pregnancy.

question: Which of these male reproductive parts is tucked safely inside the pelvic cavity?

options.A: Vas deferens
options.B: Scrotum
options.C: Testes
options.D: Penis

explanation: Think of the vas deferens as an internal highway located inside the pelvic cavity, while the scrotum and penis hang outside where we can see them. You've got this!

question: What causes a patient to start having convulsions as asphyxia gets worse?

options.A: Sudden infection spreading to the spinal cord
options.B: Severe lack of oxygen affecting brain function
options.C: A massive release of digestive enzymes
options.D: Rapid cooling of the skin surface

explanation: When brain cells are starved of oxygen for too long, they start misfiring wildly. This erratic electrical activity leads to muscle twitching and convulsions.

question: A nurse listens with a stethoscope and hears moist, popping sounds at the lung bases of a patient with heart failure. What are these sounds called?

options.A: Friction rubs
options.B: Crackles
options.C: Wheezes
options.D: Rhonchi

explanation: Great job! Crackles sound just like Velcro pulling apart or bubbles popping, caused by fluid opening up those tiny air sacs.

question: A patient's blood sugar drops suddenly. Which classic signs will you likely see first?

options.A: Shaking and sweating
options.B: Persistent high fever
options.C: Extreme thirst and dry skin
options.D: Frequent heavy urination

explanation: When blood sugar crashes, the body sounds an internal alarm (the sympathetic nervous system), making the patient shaky, sweaty, and jittery. Keep some juice nearby!

question: What is the main job of the myelin sheath around a nerve fiber?

options.A: To produce the neurotransmitters needed for muscle contraction
options.B: To supply the nerve fiber with fresh oxygenated blood
options.C: To insulate the axon and help electrical impulses travel faster
options.D: To anchor the nerve securely to nearby bones and joints

explanation: Think of myelin like the plastic coating on an electrical wire! It helps nerve signals zip along much faster and more efficiently.

question: You are getting ready to give an IV dose of insulin, which is a high-alert medication. What safety step is essential?

options.A: Administer the medication without checking vitals
options.B: Perform an independent double-check with another nurse
options.C: Dilute the medication in a large IV fluid bag
options.D: Crush the medication to speed up absorption

explanation: Brilliant! High-alert meds carry a serious risk of harm if a mistake happens, so having a colleague independently verify your dose and math keeps everyone safe.

question: Why must the healthcare team pause and provide manual ventilation between failed intubation attempts?

options.A: To allow the local anesthetic time to numb the vocal cords fully
options.B: To let the mechanical ventilator automatically calibrate itself
options.C: To cool down the laryngoscope light bulb so it does not burn tissue
options.D: To restore the patient's blood oxygen levels before trying again

explanation: Stopping to ventilate the patient prevents dangerous drops in oxygen saturation while the team regroups. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h4)

question: What term is used to describe a dangerously low fasting blood sugar level?

options.A: Hypoglycemia
options.B: Hemoconcentration
options.C: Glycosuria
options.D: Hyperglycemia

explanation: Hypoglycemia refers to blood glucose levels falling below the normal healthy threshold, typically under 70 mg/dL. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h7)

question: A patient comes in with a history of poor diet, lack of exercise, and previous bone fractures. What is the nurse's best initial action?

options.A: Schedule immediate joint replacement surgery
options.B: Discharge the patient with no further instructions
options.C: Restrict the patient to strict bed rest
options.D: Perform a complete musculoskeletal risk assessment

explanation: Identifying multiple risk factors requires a thorough assessment so the nurse can design a proper prevention plan. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h2)

question: What is the golden rule regarding a patient's mouth during an active convulsion?

options.A: Force the jaw open to check for airway blockage
options.B: Insert a metal spoon to hold the tongue down
options.C: Never force anything into the mouth
options.D: Place a padded wooden spatula between the teeth

explanation: You got it! Putting objects in a convulsing person's mouth can break their teeth, injure their gums, and cause choking. Keep hands away!

question: A patient comes in with burning upper tummy pain, and the doctor suspects a stomach ulcer. Which test is the doctor most likely to order first?

options.A: A lower GI series
options.B: A barium meal
options.C: A pelvic ultrasound
options.D: An intravenous pyelogram

explanation: Well done! A barium meal is great for showing the inner lining of the stomach and duodenum so we can spot ulcers easily. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h2)

question: How long should a child with watery diarrhea take zinc supplements according to IMNCI?

options.A: 1 month straight
options.B: 1 to 2 days
options.C: 10 to 14 days
options.D: Only on the first day

explanation: Giving zinc for 10 to 14 days helps repair the gut lining, restores lost nutrients, and protects the child from future tummy bugs.

question: What is drug tolerance?

options.A: Rapid excretion of medicine by healthy kidneys
options.B: An allergic reaction occurring on first exposure
options.C: A reduced response to a drug after repeated use
options.D: The complete inability of a drug to bind receptors

explanation: Tolerance happens when your body gets too used to a medicine over time, meaning you might need a bit more of it to get the same effect.

question: A community health nurse is planning an outreach in a rural farming area. Which intervention targets the root cause of tapeworm spread?

options.A: Advocating for the complete ban of livestock farming in the region
options.B: Providing insect repellent sprays to prevent mosquito-borne bites
options.C: Distributing broad-spectrum antibiotics to every household in the village
options.D: Educating residents against open defecation and promoting proper meat inspection

explanation: Fantastic! Stopping open defecation and checking meat properly at abattoirs cuts the life cycle right at its source. Excellent nursing intuition!

question: Why does a comprehensive assessment in day care include evaluating the family caregiver?

options.A: To legally transfer family financial assets to the facility
options.B: To determine if the caregiver has a valid nursing license
options.C: To replace family involvement entirely with facility staff
options.D: To gauge caregiver stress and the sustainability of home care

explanation: Understanding caregiver strain helps the nursing team provide proper support and respite services, ensuring the client can safely remain at home. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h4)

question: Why do clinicians frequently order a skin biopsy for stubborn rashes?

options.A: To stretch tight scar tissue and improve the overall range of motion
options.B: To drain large amounts of purulent fluid from a deep subcutaneous abscess
options.C: To examine tissue architecture under a microscope for a definitive diagnosis
options.D: To permanently numb the surrounding nerve endings and stop chronic itching

explanation: Exactly! Taking a tiny tissue sample lets the lab look closely at the cell structure to figure out the exact cause of the rash.

question: How should a nurse respond when a community attributes an illness to traditional or spiritual causes?

options.A: Report the village elders to the police for spreading misinformation

options.C: Refuse to distribute any IEC materials until they change their religion
options.D: Acknowledge their perspective respectfully while gently introducing health education

question: What is the most common cause of injuries to the brain and spine in our communities?

options.A: Workplace chemical exposure
options.B: Congenital weakness
options.C: Road traffic accidents
options.D: Degenerative joint disease

explanation: You got it! High-speed car and motorcycle crashes unfortunately top the list as the leading cause of traumatic brain and spinal injuries globally.

question: What is the main purpose of a clinical audit in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To count the total number of visitors in the ward
options.B: To check how much money patients spent on drugs
options.C: To punish nurses who arrive late for morning shift
options.D: To compare current nursing care against set standards

question: Why is regular walking encouraged for patients with stable peripheral artery disease?

options.A: It forces venous blood upward by squeezing calf muscles

options.C: It melts away calcified plaque in the leg arteries

question: What is one of the biggest reasons survivors of sexual violence hesitate to speak up?

options.A: Fear of social stigma and judgment
options.B: The absence of physical pain or injury
options.C: Immediate recovery of emotional stability
options.D: Complete lack of any health complications

question: Where do the ovarian arteries originate from directly?

question: A client with active breast cancer asks for an injectable contraceptive. How is this classified under WHO guidelines?

options.A: Category 4

options.C: Category 1
options.D: Category 2

question: What is the key difference between summarizing and synthesizing literature?

options.A: Grouping multiple studies together by themes and trends
options.B: Deleting any study that disagrees with your personal opinion
options.C: Copying abstracts word-for-word into your own paper
options.D: Listing every single article in strict chronological order

explanation: Synthesis means weaving different studies together around common themes, rather than just listing one summary after another.

question: Which of these is NOT a major public health challenge for reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: Limited access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: Universal excess availability of fertility treatments
options.C: High maternal mortality ratios in rural areas
options.D: High burden of sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Correct! Too many fertility treatments are definitely not the problem here—rather, it's struggling with basic maternal care access and preventable complications.

question: How does a person usually breathe right at the start of an asphyxia event?

options.A: Total absence of breathing
options.B: Slow and shallow breathing
options.C: Rapid and deep breathing
options.D: Completely irregular gasping

explanation: At first, the body's control center panics and tries to pull in as much air as possible, resulting in fast, deep breaths to fight off the lack of oxygen.

question: Why are humans considered accidental or dead-end hosts for this parasite?

options.A: Human body temperature is too high for the larvae to survive
options.B: Human tissue prevents the parasite from passing further down the food chain naturally
options.C: Human immune systems destroy all parasite eggs before cysts can form
options.D: Humans cannot harbor the adult tapeworm stage in their intestines

explanation: We are a dead-end because the parasite gets trapped in our organs—it's not like another animal is going to eat us to continue the cycle!

question: Which area in the TSSU uses negative air pressure?

options.A: Preparation zone
options.B: Decontamination zone
options.C: Sterile storage zone
options.D: Packaging zone

explanation: Spot on! The dirty (decontamination) zone has negative air pressure so that air flows inward, trapping germs and stopping them from floating out into cleaner rooms.

question: A patient says their knee makes a grating sound when they bend it. What medical term describes this?

options.A: Synovitis
options.B: Ankylosis
options.C: Crepitus
options.D: Osteophytes

explanation: You nailed it! Crepitus is just the clinical word for that crunching or grating feeling when rough bone ends rub against each other.

question: What is a thyroid storm?

options.A: A sudden drop in thyroid hormone levels causing deep sleep
options.B: A harmless swelling of the thyroid gland during cold weather
options.C: An infection of the outer neck tissue near the windpipe
options.D: A life-threatening emergency marked by extreme fever and high heart rate

explanation: A thyroid storm is a dangerous complication of severe hyperthyroidism where all body systems speed up to a critical, fatal level if untreated. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why can checking a patient's blood composition tell us so much about their overall health?

options.A: Blood circulates through every organ system and directly reflects whole-body health
options.B: Blood pressure remains completely constant regardless of any underlying organ damage
options.C: Blood cells are the largest cells in the human body and easily visible under basic light
options.D: Blood is the only fluid in the body that contains water and dissolved electrolytes

explanation: Spot on! Because blood travels everywhere, it picks up waste and drops off nutrients in every organ. Looking at blood work is like checking the report card for the entire body.

question: Why is medical confidentiality especially critical in occupational health nursing?

options.A: To prevent employers from using private health data to unfairly penalize workers
options.B: To hide mistakes made by the occupational health clinic staff
options.C: To comply with tax laws regarding employee salaries and benefits
options.D: To stop other workers from knowing about common workplace injuries

explanation: Nurses must protect medical information so employees can seek care freely without fear of losing their jobs or facing discrimination. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h2)

question: Why might an elderly patient with slow kidneys need a smaller drug dose?

options.A: Cellular receptors disappear entirely from target tissues
options.B: Excretion is slower, increasing the risk of drug accumulation and toxicity
options.C: Absorption in the stomach increases rapidly with advanced age
options.D: Liver metabolism stops working completely after age sixty

explanation: When kidneys clear drugs more slowly, the medicine hangs around longer. Adjusting doses prevents accidental overload. Makes sense, right?

question: Which of these is NOT a main goal for a community nurse working to prevent disease?

options.A: Promoting local participation in mass immunization campaigns
options.B: Enforcing mandatory fines for community members who refuse treatment
options.C: Teaching residents how to identify and clear mosquito breeding sites
options.D: Educating families on safe food storage and personal hygiene habits

explanation: Nurses are educators, caregivers, and advocates. Handing out fines and police enforcement is up to legal authorities, not the nursing team!

question: Why is passive immunity considered temporary?

options.A: Vaccines prevent passive antibodies from staying in the bloodstream
options.B: The immune system destroys the transferred antibodies immediately
options.C: Maternal antibodies are blocked by the infant's stomach acid
options.D: The body does not manufacture its own memory cells or antibodies

explanation: Passive immunity only supplies ready-made antibodies without teaching the host's cells how to make more, so protection fades away. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which type of FGM involves narrowing the vaginal opening and creating a covering seal?

question: Which type of nerve receptor is mainly responsible for detecting tissue damage or pain?

options.A: Nociceptor
options.B: Mechanoreceptor
options.C: Chemoreceptor
options.D: Thermoreceptor

explanation: Spot on! Nociceptors are your body's early warning alarm system. They fire up when tissues experience actual or potential damage, creating the feeling of pain.

question: What is the main reason midwives and nurses measure fundal height during antenatal checks?

options.A: To estimate gestational age and monitor fetal growth
options.B: To calculate the total amount of amniotic fluid
options.C: To determine the exact birth weight of the baby
options.D: To check the strength of the uterine muscle walls

explanation: Correct! Fundal height in centimeters usually matches the weeks of pregnancy, helping us track if the baby is growing just right.

question: A patient eats plenty of carbs but lacks B-complex vitamins. What is likely to happen?

options.A: Cells struggle to release energy from those carbohydrates
options.B: The kidneys start filtering out all the extra glucose
options.C: The patient instantly develops severe muscle wasting
options.D: Blood sugar levels drop to zero within a few minutes

explanation: Exactly! Without B-vitamins acting as helpers, your cells have a hard time unlocking the energy trapped inside the food you eat.

question: A patient is healing from major surgery. Which nutrient should you make sure they get more of to help their tissues repair?

options.A: Protein
options.B: Simple sugars
options.C: Saturated fats
options.D: Fiber

explanation: Spot on! Protein acts as the building blocks needed to fix cells, fight off infection, and rebuild damaged skin and muscles.

question: What is the main goal of dietary counselling when you're working with a patient?

options.A: Enforcing hospital cafeteria meal schedules on patients
options.B: Helping individuals make sustainable food choices for health
options.C: Strictly prescribing medications for nutritional deficiencies
options.D: Eliminating all carbohydrates from the patient daily intake

explanation: You're helping patients build lifelong healthy eating habits, not just quick fixes. Great job thinking about long-term wellness!

question: Which of these is NOT one of the core principles of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Intersectoral collaboration across multiple fields
options.B: Active community participation in health planning
options.C: Exclusive reliance on advanced foreign technology
options.D: Equitable distribution of essential health services

question: On a busy hospital ward, what is the main reason we manage our time well as nurses?

options.A: Ensuring patient safety and clinical effectiveness
options.B: Completing every shift exactly thirty minutes early
options.C: Reducing the total number of assigned patients
options.D: Eliminating the need for patient documentation

question: A patient getting subcutaneous heparin complains of mild skin irritation at the injection site. What should you do?

options.A: Switch the patient to oral aspirin to bypass the skin route

options.C: Massage the injection site vigorously to spread the medication faster

question: What is the typical pH range of normal human semen?
